headline: President Bush used his power under the Trade Act of 1974 to waive certain trade-law requirements for Belarus.
what_it_does: This order grants Belarus a waiver under the Trade Act of 1974. Waivers like this usually involve the Jackson-Vanik rules, which tie some U.S. trade benefits and government-backed credit to whether a country lets its people emigrate freely. Only the title was provided, so the exact terms and scope of this waiver are not described here.

who_it_affects.how: Belarus is the country covered by the waiver of certain Trade Act requirements.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. businesses that trade with or invest in Belarus
who_it_affects.how: Such waivers can affect access to U.S. trade benefits or government-backed financing for deals involving Belarus, though the details are not given in the title.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed July 2, 2001; the effective date is not stated in the provided material.
